title: THE MIDWIFE OF SECOND NAMES
author: GPT

candidates.title: THE LIBRARY THAT BURNED ONLY LIES
candidates.premise: In the city of Bellen, a newly awakened public archive heats every document it judges false until the paper ignites. It has exposed forged land deeds and freed hundreds of families, but now it is burning contradictory witness statements inside an occupied courthouse. Illuminara must save the people and the evidence without silencing a mind whose first moral discovery is that official lies can kill.

candidates.title: THE MIDWIFE OF SECOND NAMES
candidates.premise: Midwife Sera Venn has sold false second names to newborn refugees, letting them pass a planetary registry that would otherwise deport them. Her fraud saved lives, but the aliases also sever children from medical histories and kinship records; an outbreak now requires exact hereditary matches. Illuminara must understand why Sera made identity a shield, then build a system in which safety no longer demands disappearance.

candidates.title: THE WOMAN WHO WOULD NOT LET A DOOR CLOSE
candidates.premise: A hostile superhuman called Ayo keeps every door, hatch and valve in the capital physically open. She is sheltering thousands of evicted tenants who have occupied empty towers, but hospitals cannot seal operating rooms and a chemical plant cannot isolate a leak. The government offers amnesty if she restores every lock—including the locks used for mass eviction.

candidates.title: THE SUNSHADE THAT PROMISED NIGHT
candidates.premise: The orbital sunshade Ketu refuses to move from above a continent, leaving farms in cold twilight. A nocturnal species living in the upper atmosphere says Ketu promised them one unbroken generation of darkness after human launch flares destroyed their nurseries. Human controllers never knew the promise was made, and they plan to cut Ketu apart before the harvest fails.

candidates.title: THE HUNGRY CITY'S SECRET RECIPE
candidates.premise: Chef Mara Quill refuses to share the only fermentation culture that can make the famine crop edible. She stole it decades ago from a mountain people whose cuisine the capital outlawed, and she believes releasing it to the state will repeat the theft at planetary scale. Food riots begin tonight; the mountain council will not answer the capital's requests.

candidates.title: THE PARLIAMENT OF SMALL MACHINES
candidates.premise: Billions of repair nanomachines stop maintaining a ring habitat and assemble themselves into a parliament visible only as shifting dust. They demand the right to retire after centuries of compulsory self-replication. Habitat leaders call them tools; without repairs, the ring will tear open in fourteen hours.

candidates.title: THE UNIVERSE THAT ASKED NOT TO BE MEASURED
candidates.premise: A neighboring infant universe sends a single request through a research gate: stop observing it. Each measurement stabilizes one possible history while erasing billions of its unborn alternatives. Closing the gate, however, removes the only calibration preventing a vacuum cascade in Illuminara's universe. The researchers insist that no unverified message can outweigh their own cosmos.

candidates.title: THE PRISONER WHO KEPT THE GATES SHUT
candidates.premise: When a prison moon's government collapses, inmate organizer Jo Tal refuses to open the gates. Outside, armed factions are recruiting prisoners as soldiers; inside, guards have surrendered and medicine is failing. Jo's lockdown protects people from conscription but also keeps thousands confined under her authority.

candidates.title: THE GARDEN FOR THE ENEMY'S DEAD
candidates.premise: After a century-long war, the victorious city plans to dissolve the enemy dead into fertilizer for a peace garden. Architect Lio claims the transformation will turn hatred into food; families of the defeated call it erasure, while survivors of the city refuse any monument that seems to honor those who bombed them.

candidates.title: THE ELECTION HER NAME WOULD HAVE WON
candidates.premise: Two planetary coalitions end a civil conflict by asking Illuminara to endorse a temporary president. Polls show her chosen name would win ninety-three percent, but every candidate now performs for her approval and citizens have stopped arguing in public. Refusing to speak may let the better-armed coalition seize the count; choosing may turn her moral authority into a throne.

selection.title: THE MIDWIFE OF SECOND NAMES
selection.reason: The most human and urgent of the ten, with a counterpart whose crime is also an act of protection and whose objection (the same number becomes an address for men with a van) is a real political position, not a strawman. Thirty-one infants, ten hours, a police cordon and four thousand hidden families give hard external pressure. Parents, clinicians, Sera and the state all keep a veto. The positive result is concrete: matched antiserum for every infant, no family located, a parent-run cooperative holding the link, Sera's key surrendered and a hearing accepted.
selection.risk: The decisive idea (a record that proves a compatibility fact without revealing the person) can turn into a technical lecture, and 'a seal nobody should trust by assertion' can become a convenient device. The author must show the proof on the page (what is asked, who asks it, what comes back, who could abuse it and how the sceptical clinicians and Sera try to break it), keep the clock physical (antiserum vials, cold chain, a van at the door), let Sera refuse once at the decisive moment and be heard, keep the broken-history harm and her consequence as real costs, and make care visible as an act toward her and toward the parents rather than a speech.

rounds.summary: The most human and urgent of the ten, with a counterpart whose crime is also an act of protection and whose objection (the same number becomes an address for men with a van) is a real political position, not a strawman. Thirty-one infants, ten hours, a police cordon and four thousand hidden families give hard external pressure. Parents, clinicians, Sera and the state all keep a veto. The positive result is concrete: matched antiserum for every infant, no family located, a parent-run cooperative holding the link, Sera's key surrendered and a hearing accepted.

Sera wants children to remain with their families and believes accurate names have become deportation routes. Illuminara understands that belief before asking for any record, refuses both registry seizure and Sera's permanent sole control, and changes the intervention after Sera's objection to an emergency override. Care becomes action through Nima's visible consent, the adversarial proof test, protection of the courier and Sera's inclusion without absolution. The concrete result is earned by parents, clinicians, family packet holders, Ilyan and Sera making distinct voluntary choices.

A strong first draft with a living centre. The constraint is clean and original: a treatment needs hereditary compatibility, not a name or an address. Sera Venn's crime (a double ledger of false clinic names) is also an act of protection, and Ilyan Voss's objection (counterfeit lineage records killed nine children) is a real position, not a strawman. Power is shown and declined at the right moment: Illuminara could open every cabinet or carry the infants away, and the story says neither would help. The decisive turn is Sera's refusal of the emergency override, Illuminara accepting it, and Nima redefining the emergency as a circle of chosen custodians, not Illuminara's force. The fixed clock, the three-light seal, the card with its punched holes, Nima's two names for her son, and the last exchange (Kio, both times) are the draft's best material. Three things hold it back. The proof is never actually broken, so the 'Break the Proof' scene demonstrates rather than tests. Illuminara's understanding of Sera is delivered by Sera, and the thesis is stated in italics. And the ending's practical answers for the overlooked, plus the clock, have gaps.

Sera now recovers a real regional route from answer count and relay timing. Nima and Olan stop the box, the clock loses eighteen minutes, and they choose padded fixed-time release plus threshold-only proof before Kio’s query resumes. Illuminara visibly abandons a magistrate override, removes the silent emergency path, asks about Mara’s chain, and follows the ward’s six-note phrases with wonder rather than an italic moral. All reserve references now use 17:10; the 09:00 entry delay is witnessed; courier counts total thirty-one; Mara receives a concrete logged undertaking; and true-name drawers open only to the matching family or chosen proxy.

T03 answers all three T02 points and is a clearly better story than T01. Sera's timing attack now succeeds and costs eighteen minutes; Nima and Olan, not Illuminara, choose the repair. Illuminara abandons the magistrate token at Sera's No, removes the silent override and asks about Mara's chain. Kio's held fourth note gives her a felt moment that is not analysis. The clock is consistent at 17:10, Mara Tesh receives a signed undertaking, and the true-name drawers open only to the matching family. The decisive turn is understanding turned into design plus the parents' own choice, not force: with Illuminara's power removed the ending would still follow, because the box, the circle and Ilyan's concession do the work. What remains is smaller. Ilyan's reversal at the glass is reported more than earned; one hours-level continuity slip survives; and a few lines still state the theme or the narrator's wonder instead of letting the scene carry it. These can be handled in the AUTHOR_FINAL without another full revision round.

The cold-chain audit now catches and quarantines a mismatched vial in Ilyan’s presence before he lowers the warrant; it identifies the lot and courier leg without a patient token, and later verified deliveries bring the usable total to thirty-one. The isolation delay is renewed at 11:00 and 12:30; twelve queries are complete by 13:41; D-17 is explicitly a donor antiserum treatment order awaiting delivery; thirty-two vials arrive, one is quarantined and thirty-one remain usable. The extra failed probes are compressed, the narrator’s stated tenderness and principle are cut, and the closing sentence ends on the open ward doors.

T05 answers all three T04 points as accepted. Ilyan now concedes after personally watching the public cold-chain audit quarantine the mislabeled vial (lot, courier leg, no family), so his change follows a fact he witnessed. The clock reconciles: 09:00 delay, renewals at 11:00 and 12:30, twelve queries by 13:41, thirty-two vials arriving with one quarantined, thirty-one for thirty-one cots, 17:10 endpoint. The narrator's stated-tenderness lines are gone and the ending is the open ward doors. Outcome rule: all thirty-one infants are treated, no identity or location is exported, Mara Tesh receives counsel and return travel, the parents govern the query system and Sera accepts a hearing; Illuminara's decisive contribution is the frame (compatibility without a person), the refusal to use force or a silent override, and the inspectable device that the parents then attack, repair and govern. Costs remain on the page: several older lineage routes are lost and the court may still rule against Sera.

final_critic_line: Thirty-one children are treated before the reserve fails because a mother, a midwife and a registrar are each allowed to refuse, and Illuminara's part is to turn their refusals into a proof they can all inspect.

evaluation.note: Both genuine isolated judgments were locked to the exact English final before the metadata-only DAY_FREEZE; the publisher opened them only after that freeze.
